draft.title: Chronology and dating
card: Chronology means putting events in the order they happened. Historians show this on a timeline, with earlier events on the left and later events on the right.
BCE
"Before Common Era". Years are counted backwards towards year 1, so 500 BCE is earlier than 100 BCE.
CE
"Common Era". Years are counted forwards from year 1, so 100 CE is earlier than 500 CE. There is no year 0.
Centuries
A century is 100 years. Centuries are counted from year 1, so years 1 to 100 are the 1st century. The 1400s are the 15th century, and the 1800s are the 19th century.
draft.remember: Order events on a timeline. BCE counts down to year 1, CE counts up from it, and the 1400s are the 15th century.

a.q: Which list puts these dates in order, from earliest to latest?
opts: 300 BCE, 50 BCE, 40 CE, 200 CE
50 BCE, 300 BCE, 40 CE, 200 CE
40 CE, 200 CE, 50 BCE, 300 BCE
200 CE, 40 CE, 50 BCE, 300 BCE
a.why: BCE years count down towards year 1, so 300 BCE comes before 50 BCE. All BCE dates come before CE dates, and CE years count up. The second list is tempting but wrongly puts 50 BCE before 300 BCE, as if BCE years counted up.
a.clue: For BCE years, a bigger number means further back in time.

b.q: A museum in Ballarat has a coin made in 1465. A student writes that it is from the 14th century. What is the mistake?
opts: The 1400s are the 15th century, so it is from the 15th
The 1400s are the 14th century, but it should say BCE
Centuries are counted from year 0, so it is the 16th
A coin from 1465 is too old to be given a century
b.why: Centuries are counted from year 1, so years 1401 to 1500 are the 15th century. The student matched the number in 1400s to the century, which is the common slip. The BCE option is wrong because 1465 is a CE year, counted forwards.
b.clue: The 1st century is years 1 to 100. Count up from there.

b.best: The 1400s are the 15th century, so it is from the 15th

problems.detail: Why (a) names a wrong option by position ('The second list is tempting'). Options appear in random order, so the position will not match what students see. It may even point to the correct list, which is second in this order. Name the option by its content instead (50 BCE, 300 BCE, 40 CE, 200 CE).

The card says 'The 1400s are the 15th century', but Why (b) says the 15th century is years 1401 to 1500. Strictly, the year 1400 is in the 14th century and 1500 is in the 15th. A careful student may see these as clashing. Consider adding a short note that '1400s' is the everyday way of saying it.

check.summary: Both answers are clear and correct. Why (a) refers to 'the second list', which will not match the shuffled order. There is also a small mismatch between 'the 1400s are the 15th century' on the card and '1401 to 1500' in Why (b).
